Counsel for Applicant :- Ramakar Shukla,Abhinav Singh

Hon'ble Subhash Vidyarthi,J.
1. Heard Sri Ramakar Shukla, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Hari Shankar Maurya, learned Addl. Government Advocate, and perused the record.

2. By means of the instant application the applicant Manjesh S/o Ram Kishun Pasi seeks bail in Case Crime No. 190 of 2022, under section 376, I.P.C., and section 3/4, Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, P.S. Sursa, District Hardoi.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
3. The aforesaid case has been registered on the basis of a First Information Report (F.I.R.) lodged on 15.05.2022 alleging that the applicant had raped the informant's daughter at about 8 p.m. on 14.05.2022.
4.
In the medico-legal examination report of the victim no mark of injury has been reported on any part of her body and no definite opinion has been given about the alleged sexual assault.

sentences.text: 5. Statement of the victim has been recorded by the Trial Court and although she has supported the F.I.R. version in her examination-in-chief, in her cross-examination she categorically declined from the incident.
6. In the affidavit filed in support of the bail-application it has been stated that the applicant is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated in the present case and he has no criminal history.
7. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the bail-application, but could not dispute the aforesaid facts.

8. Having considered the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the facts that the allegations are not supported either by the medico-legal examination report or by the statement of the victim having already been recorded, in case of the applicant's release, he will not be in a position to influence the victim, without making any observation, which may affect the merits of the case, I am of the view that the aforesaid facts are sufficient for making out a case for enlargement of the applicant on bail.
9. Accordingly, this bail application stands allowed.

10. Let the applicantManjesh S/o Ram Kishun Pasi be released on bail in the aforesaid Case Crime No. 190 of 2022, under section 376, I.P.C., and section 3/4, Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, P.S. Sursa, District Hardoi, on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of Magistrate/Court concerned.
11.

sentences.text:
Before parting with this case, it is observed that in Hariom Sharma v. State of U.P., 2022 (120)
ACC 251, a coordinate Bench of this Court had held as under:-
"10......Neither accused nor victim or any witnesses should be permitted to subvert a criminal trial by stating falsehood and resort to contrivances, so as to make it theatre of the absurd.

entities.text:
Hariom Sharma v. State of U.P., 2022 (120)
ACC 251
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Dispensation of justice in a criminal trial is a serious issue and cannot be allowed to become a mockery by simply allowing prime prosecution witnesses /victims to turn hostile as a ground of acquittal.

Complainants should also be accountable and should take responsibility on their shoulder."
12.
Considering the societal interest, it is high time for the trial court to resort to Section 344 Cr.P.C in appropriate cases.

In the present case since the prosecutrix before the trial Court has turned hostile and completely denied the prosecution version, therefore she is not entitled to the benefit of any compensation paid by the Government, which has been collected from the taxpayers of the country.

13. In view of the above, trial Court shall consider the issuance of necessary direction against the alleged prosecutrix/ victim to refund the amount of compensation, if any, received by her, in the appropriate head of the treasury account and shall also ensure the compliance of provisions of section 344 Cr.P.C at the appropriate stage, if it deems fit and proper under the facts and circumstances of the case.

15. In the present case also the victim/ informant levelled an allegation of rape but subsequently she turned hostile and said that the alleged offence did not take place.
16. The trial court is directed to take action as per the aforesaid direction issued by this Court, in present matter also.
